items.title: USN-9201-1: NetworkManager vulnerability
items.summary: Juthawong Naisanguansee discovered that NetworkManager on Ubuntu incorrectly granted the whoopsie user unrestricted D-Bus access to root-only methods. A local attacker who can execute code as the whoopsie user could possibly use this issue to disrupt system networking or alter NetworkManager logging

items.title: USN-9200-1: elfutils vulnerabilities
items.summary: It was discovered that elfutils incorrectly handled memory when processing certain malformed DWARF data. items.title: USN-9199-1: authd vulnerability
items.summary: Adrian Dombeck discovered that authd incorrectly assigned user and group identifiers during first-time SSH logins. A remote authenticated user could possibly use this issue to access or modify files belonging to another user, potentially leading to account takeover or privilege escalation.

items.title: USN-9197-1: Speex vulnerability
items.summary: It was discovered that Speex incorrectly handled oversize input when appending data to a bit buffer not owned by the library. An attacker could possibly use this issue to cause Speex to crash, resulting in a denial of service, or possibly execute arbitrary code.

items.title: USN-9196-1: Expat vulnerabilities
items.summary: It was discovered that Expat did not properly validate UTF-16 surrogate pairs. items.title: USN-9193-1: PCRE vulnerability
items.summary: Yunho Kim discovered that PCRE incorrectly handled memory when processing certain regular expressions with JIT compilation enabled. An attacker could possibly use this issue to cause applications using PCRE to expose sensitive information.
